observations.text: SP maintained basic aircraft control to the level required by this training section, with the IP directing the pitch and power changes during the climb and level off. Altitude excursions reached 400 feet and airspeed 25 KIAS before the IP's direction restored the assigned parameters. Performance is marginal for the block; an independent instrument cross-check and earlier recognition of the deviation trend are expected to improve.

SP, working to the IP's verbal prompts, completed the climb, level off and level flight segments with the flight parameters returned to the assigned values. Altitude was held within 300 feet, airspeed within 20 KIAS and heading within 10 degrees, and the corrections, although applied with delay, were correct. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP set engine power appropriately for the climb and the descent and used the trim to relieve control pressures without prompting. Altitude was held within 200 feet, airspeed within 15 KIAS and heading within 7 degrees, the minor deviations being recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the aircraft with comfort and ease, maintaining altitude within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 KIAS and heading within 4 degrees during climbs, descents, level offs and turns up to 30 degrees of bank. Trim was used correctly across the airspeed range and power was set accurately for each phase of flight, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the aircraft on instruments with exceptional precision, holding altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 KIAS and heading within 2 degrees in every phase of flight, including turns up to 30 degrees of bank. Aircraft switches and trim were handled flawlessly and the radio aids were used throughout to maintain orientation. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a trim technique that left continuous elevator pressure during the climb, did not handle the aircraft with comfort and ease and did not set climb power as required to maintain the flight parameters. Altitude diverged by more than 300 feet and airspeed by more than 20 KIAS from the briefed climb speed, with the result that the IP directed the pitch and power corrections and flew part of the level off. Further practice in trim and power management during climbs is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, interrupted the instrument cross-check during the descent and did not adjust power to hold the descent parameters. Airspeed increased 25 KIAS above the briefed value and the aircraft passed the assigned altitude by 400 feet, with the result that the IP took control to re-establish the descent. Restoration of the scan immediately after any cockpit indication is required.

SP maintained basic aircraft control to the level required by this training section, completing the level flight and turn segments after the IP's verbal prompts. Altitude was held at the 300 foot limit and heading at 10 degrees of deviation, and the corrections, although correct, were applied with delay. Performance is marginal for the block; earlier recognition of the deviation trend is expected to improve with further practice.

SP controlled engine power appropriately for each phase of flight and held altitude within 200 feet, airspeed within 15 KIAS and heading within 8 degrees through the climb, the level off and turns up to 30 degrees of bank. The minor deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled the aircraft with comfort and ease, trimming accurately across the airspeed range and setting power correctly for each phase of flight. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 6 KIAS and heading within 3 degrees during climbs, descents, level flight and turns up to 30 degrees of bank. Corrections were accurate and prompt, with no intervention by the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated an instrument cross-check well above the level expected for this training section, holding altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 KIAS and heading within 2 degrees in all phases of flight. Aileron, elevator and rudder trim were handled flawlessly and the radio aids were used to maintain orientation without any degradation of the scan. Deviations were negligible throughout the sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to power settings applied without reference to the phase of flight, did not maintain the briefed descent parameters and attempted to control airspeed with the elevator alone. Airspeed diverged by 25 KIAS and the aircraft descended 450 feet through the assigned altitude, with the result that the IP directed the recovery and set the power. Study of the power settings prescribed by the Flight Manual for each phase of flight is required.

SP, due to a degraded basic instrument scan, did not cross-check the attitude indicator against the performance instruments during the turns up to 30 degrees of bank and did not maintain the assigned parameters. Heading deviation reached 20 degrees and altitude 400 feet with an unrecognized nose-low attitude, with the result that the IP took control to recover the aircraft. Re-establishment of a systematic instrument cross-check is required.

SP, due to late and coarse elevator inputs at the level off, did not anticipate the lead point and did not reduce power at the correct time. Altitude overshoot reached 300 feet and airspeed 20 KIAS above the briefed level flight value, with the result that the assigned parameters were regained only after the IP's verbal prompts. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not sustain the instrument cross-check during the turn to the assigned heading. Heading deviation reached 10 degrees and altitude 300 feet, at the limit of the standards, with the result that the parameters were regained only after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation and the corrective input were both delayed.

SP maintained airspeed, altitude and heading within the standards of this training section during climbs, descents and turns up to 30 degrees of bank. Deviations reached 250 feet in altitude and 15 KIAS twice at the level off, each recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention. Performance is marginal for the block; a tighter altitude capture and an earlier power reduction are expected to improve.

SP handled the aircraft and its switches with comfort and ease, trimming correctly in the full airspeed range and setting power as required for each phase of flight. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 7 KIAS and heading within 4 degrees throughout the climb, descent, level flight and turn segments. Corrections were accurate and prompt, without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the aircraft on instruments with exceptional accuracy, holding altitude within 50 feet, airspeed within 3 KIAS and heading within 2 degrees in all phases of flight, including turns up to 30 degrees of bank. SP also used the radio aids continuously to maintain orientation and remained ahead of the aircraft throughout the sortie. Deviations were negligible and no prompting was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to uncoordinated aileron and rudder inputs that were left untrimmed in the turns, did not handle the aircraft with comfort and ease and did not hold the assigned altitude through the reversals. Altitude excursion reached 500 feet and heading deviation 20 degrees on roll-out, with the result that the IP intervened on the controls to re-establish level flight. Further practice in trim technique during turns is required.

SP, due to a false attitude perception that was not resolved against the instruments, did not transition promptly to the flight instruments after entering cloud and did not maintain the assigned climb parameters. The aircraft diverged 450 feet in altitude and 25 degrees in heading, with a bank in excess of 30 degrees that went unrecognized, with the result that the IP took control and recovered the aircraft. Immediate reference to the attitude indicator on entering IMC is required.

SP, due to a scan that dwelt on the altimeter at the expense of the attitude indicator, did not detect the developing pitch change in level flight and did not adjust power in time. Altitude deviation reached 300 feet and airspeed 20 KIAS, at the limit of the standards, with the result that level flight was restored only after the IP's verbal prompts. Errors were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the assigned heading, did not maintain the instrument cross-check and did not correct the developing heading drift. Heading deviation reached 10 degrees and altitude 280 feet, with the result that the assigned parameters were regained after the IP's verbal prompts. Recognition of the deviation and the corrective input were delayed.

SP, due to power changes made after rather than together with the attitude change, produced repeated small airspeed oscillations in the transitions from climb to level flight. Airspeed varied by 15 KIAS and altitude by 200 feet at the level off, each deviation being recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the navigation display, did not hold the assigned heading through the turn at 30 degrees of bank. Heading deviation reached 8 degrees and altitude 200 feet, with the result of minor deviations that SP recognized and corrected without the IP's intervention. The cross-check was re-established without prompting.

SP maintained altitude within 140 feet, airspeed within 9 KIAS and heading within 4 degrees through climbs, descents, level offs and turns up to 30 degrees of bank, using the trim correctly across the airspeed range. The values remained inside the standards of this training section but sat close to their limits during the descent segment. Performance is marginal for the block; a steadier cross-check rate is expected to consolidate the parameters well inside the tolerances.

SP handled the aircraft and its switches flawlessly, trimming accurately in the full airspeed range and setting power precisely for every phase of flight. Altitude was held within 40 feet, airspeed within 3 KIAS and heading within 2 degrees through climbs, descents, level flight and turns up to 30 degrees of bank, while the radio aids were used throughout to maintain orientation. Deviations were negligible and no prompting by the IP was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.
